Third-party viewer libraries, self-hosted so PClinic works under its own
Content-Security-Policy and on a clinic LAN without internet.

cornerstone-core 2.6.1            MIT   https://github.com/cornerstonejs/cornerstone
cornerstone-math 0.1.10           MIT   https://github.com/cornerstonejs/cornerstoneMath
cornerstone-tools 6.0.10          MIT   https://github.com/cornerstonejs/cornerstoneTools
hammer.js 2.0.8                   MIT   https://github.com/hammerjs/hammer.js
dicom-parser 1.8.21               MIT   https://github.com/cornerstonejs/dicomParser
cornerstone-wado-image-loader 4.13.2 (NoWebWorkers bundle: JPEG baseline/lossless,
  JPEG-LS (CharLS), JPEG 2000 (OpenJPEG), HTJ2K (OpenJPH), RLE decoders inlined)
                                  MIT   https://github.com/cornerstonejs/cornerstoneWADOImageLoader

PClinic modifications to cornerstoneWADOImageLoader.bundle.min.js (kept minimal, marked "PClinic patch"):
  1. The 1.2 MB inline copy of the decode worker source was removed; the worker is
     always started from vendor/index.worker.bundle.min.worker.js.
  2. The worker factory starts the worker from that file URL first. The library's
     default blob:/data: inline worker is blocked *silently* by a strict
     Content-Security-Policy (no exception is thrown), which left every decode
     task hanging. A URL worker carries its own CSP (see firebase.json), so the
     page itself never needs 'unsafe-eval'.
